newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki closes up as cyclicals ignore weaker dollar.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki closes up as cyclicals ignore weaker dollar.

text.p: Finnish cyclical stocks with engineering group Rauma and forest industry companies in the lead ignored a weaker dollar and pulled the Helsinki bourse to a marginally higher close on Friday, brokers said.
The HEX all-share index closed 0.15 percent up at 3,006.65 points. For the week, the HEX index advanced 34.2 points or 1.1 percent.
Volume was thin on Friday at 400 million markka as many operators extended the Ascension Thursday holiday into a long weekend.
Rauma rose 5.5 percent in lively demand following main owner UPM-Kymmene's decision earlier in the week to cut its stake in Rauma through an offering of shares, brokers said.

Forestries outperformed, boosted by big overnight gains in U.S. paper stocks and in anticipation of earnings reports -- Metsa-Serla is due to release first-quarter earnings on Monday and UPM-Kymmene's report is due out on Thursday.
Telecoms blue-chip Nokia closed 3.00 markka lower at 325.00 markka, accounting for a good third of total turnover.

Banks underperformed and Merita, Finland's biggest banking group, extended Wednesday's losses after reporting a sharp rise in January-March earnings, mainly based, however, on gains from a downsizing of its equity portfolio.
